title: Uncovering the Tells: Efficient Black-Box Audits for LLM Data Contamination
abstract: arXiv:2611.30639v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Existing methods for assessing training data contamination in Large Language Models achieve high accuracy, but fundamentally rely on gray-box access, rendering them inapplicable to fully black-box environments. This limitation forces auditors to rely on full-sequence sampling or rigid heuristics, both of which incur prohibitive inference costs and struggle to isolate the underlying memorization signal. To overcome this, we propose a generation-based black-box framework that infers context-induced information gain from targeted token discrepancies. We introduce a budget-constrained auditing regime, building on the empirical observation that the membership signal is highly sparse and concentrated in a few highly informative tokens. We formalize this sparsity, showing why uniform sampling needs many more samples than a policy that targets informative positions. Empirically, our approach achieves state-of-the-art black-box separation accur

translated_title: 揭示痕迹：面向大语言模型数据污染的高效黑盒审计
translated_abstract: 现有的评估大语言模型训练数据污染的方法虽然能达到很高的准确率，但从根本上依赖于灰盒访问，使其无法应用于完全黑盒的环境。这一局限迫使审计者只能依赖全序列采样或僵化的启发式方法，二者都会带来高昂的推理成本，且难以分离出潜在的记忆信号。为了克服这一问题，我们提出了一种基于生成的黑盒框架，通过有针对性的 token 差异来推断上下文引起的信息增益。我们引入了一种预算受限的审计机制，其建立在这样一个经验观察之上：成员信号高度稀疏，并集中在少数信息量极大的 token 上。我们对这种稀疏性进行了形式化证明，说明了为什么均匀采样需要比针对信息丰富位置的策略多得多的样本。在实证方面，我们的方法实现了最先进的黑盒区分准确率……
tldr: 该论文提出了一个基于生成的黑盒审计框架，利用训练数据成员信号高度稀疏并集中于少数高信息量 token 的特性，进行预算受限的针对性 token 采样，从而在不依赖灰盒访问的情况下高效准确地审计大语言模型的训练数据污染。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes a generation-based black-box audit framework that exploits the observation that membership signals are highly sparse and concentrated in a few informative tokens, enabling budget-constrained targeted token sampling for efficient and accurate auditing of LLM training data contamination without gray-box access.
